answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: Anne Frank wrote this in her essay “Give!” on 26 March 1944 while hiding in the Secret Annex — a piece later collected in Tales from the Secret Annex, not in her famous Diary. Wikiquote lists it among her sourced writings ↗. The exact popular English wording is one of a few close translation variants of the same passage.

source.heading: The source: an essay called “Give!”, not the Diary

source.excerpt: “How wonderful it is that no one has to wait, but can start right now to gradually change the world! How wonderful it is that everyone, great and small, can immediately help bring about justice by giving of themselves! … You can always — always — give something, even if it’s a simple act of kindness!”
trail: Wikiquote places the line in its sourced section, citing the essay “Give!” dated 26 March 1944.
The Trafficking Institute’s #InContext series independently traces the quote to Anne’s essay “Give!” of 26 March 1944.
The essay was published in Tales from the Secret Annex; the USHMM catalog record confirms the English translation by Ralph Manheim and Michel Mok (1983).
The Anne Frank House notes she filled a notebook with tales, essays and reminiscences while in hiding — the body of work this essay belongs to.
source.excerptNote: From the essay “Give!” (26 March 1944), in the Ralph Manheim & Michel Mok translation. The widely-circulated popular form of the opening line — “How wonderful it is that nobody need wait a single moment before starting to improve the world” — is a looser paraphrase of this same passage.

author.name: Anne Frank
author.heading: Anne Frank
author.bio: Anne Frank was a German-born Jewish girl who, from 1942 to 1944, hid with her family from Nazi persecution in a concealed annex in Amsterdam. Alongside her celebrated diary she filled a separate notebook with short stories, fables and essays — among them “Give!”, the source of this line. She was deported and died in the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp in early 1945, aged 15; her writings were published posthumously by her father, Otto Frank.

misattribution.heading: Right author, wrong book
misattribution.intro: The attribution to Anne Frank is correct — but two things are routinely garbled about this line.

items.why: It is constantly quoted as coming from The Diary of a Young Girl. It does not appear there. It comes from a separate essay, “Give!”, written 26 March 1944 and later collected in Tales from the Secret Annex ↗.

“…before starting to improve the world” is one of several near-identical English renderings; Wikiquote ↗ also records “…before beginning to improve the world” and “no one has to wait, but can start right now to gradually change the world.” All translate the same genuine Dutch sentence.

misattribution.truthLine: Bottom line: genuinely Anne Frank’s words — from her essay “Give!” of 26 March 1944, not her Diary — as documented here ↗.

context.heading: Written in hiding, weeks before capture
lead: Anne Frank wrote “Give!” on 26 March 1944, roughly four months before the annex was raided and its occupants deported. The essay is a plea for generosity and human dignity — she argues that no one is too small or too poor to give, if only kindness, and that improving the world can begin instantly.
That the line comes from a teenager in hiding, writing about improving a world that was actively trying to destroy her, is a large part of why it resonates — and why it is worth quoting accurately.
detailsBody: Between roughly September 1943 and May 1944 Anne kept a stiff-backed notebook of stories, fables and essays distinct from her diary. These were first published in Dutch in 1949 and, in expanded form, in 1960; the English collection Tales from the Secret Annex followed, translated by Ralph Manheim and Michel Mok.
context.pull: You can always, always give something, even if it is only kindness.
